analysis.title: Uranium Energy Corp. (UEC): Long-term utility contracts provide sales visibility while preserving unhedged exposure
key_insights: UEC announced two long-term sales agreements with U.S. nuclear utilities covering 1.1mn lbs of U3O8 over six years, with deliveries beginning in 2027.
All deliveries are priced at prevailing spot market prices with no floors, ceilings, discounts or fixed pricing, so UEC keeps its unhedged exposure to uranium prices.
GS views the agreements positively: they add visibility into future sales while preserving upside from a tightening uranium market.

The contracts follow management commentary that utility contracting activity was increasing and that UEC was seeing traction on proposals without price caps or discounts, which GS calls a positive divergence from typical contracting.
One contract provides 100k lbs/year from 2027-2032 and the other 100k lbs/year from 2028-2032.
At about $92/lb uranium, the two contracts equal about $100mn of revenue potential, about $9mn in 2027 and about $18mn per year in 2028-2032.
GS/FactSet consensus revenue is $52mn in 2027 and $264mn in 2028, so the contracts cover a small share of expected sales. GS forecasts UEC sales of 550k lbs in FY2027 and 2.5mn lbs in FY2028.
UEC remains in discussions with other U.S. and international utilities for additional contracts.
The NNSA has outlined a need for 4mn lbs/year of unobligated U.S.-origin uranium beginning as early as 2030, which UEC believes it can support as its Texas and Wyoming production ramps.
GS rates UEC Buy with a 12-month price target of $14, based on 22.5X EV/EBITDA on F2029 EBITDA estimates, implying 94.7% upside from $7.19.

market_movers.rationale: Long-term spot-priced utility contracts add sales visibility while keeping unhedged uranium price exposure. Target is 22.5X EV/EBITDA on F2029 EBITDA.

earnings_insights: UEC F2026 (FY ended 7/26) average realized price was $93.13/lb under its unhedged strategy.
GS forecasts UEC to sell 550k lbs in FY2027 and 2.5mn lbs in FY2028.
The report states GS/FactSet consensus revenue of $52mn for 2027 and $264mn for 2028, and the cover table shows matching GS estimates.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Used to value the contracts at about $100mn of revenue potential. GS describes the uranium market as tightening.
Potential U.S. government demand that UEC believes it can support as production ramps.

risk_factors: Uranium prices remaining volatile or subdued.
Timing and pace of the production ramp remain uncertain.
Greater liquidity needs causing continued dilution.
